authoredSolutions.80: The hexagon has perimeter \(6s\), so the square has perimeter \(20-6s\) and side \(\frac{10-3s}{2}\). The combined area is \(A=\left(\frac{10-3s}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}s^{2}\). Setting \(\frac{dA}{ds}=-\frac{3(10-3s)}{2}+3\sqrt{3}\,s=0\) gives \(2\sqrt{3}\,s=10-3s\), so \(s=\frac{10}{3+2\sqrt{3}}\). Since \(\frac{d^{2}A}{ds^{2}}>0\), this is the minimum. Hence (D).
authoredSolutions.85: Completing the square, \(x^{2}+x+1=\left(x+\tfrac12\right)^{2}+\tfrac34\). With \(u=x+\tfrac12,\ k=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), \(\int\frac{du}{(u^{2}+k^{2})^{2}}=\frac{1}{2k^{2}}\left[\frac{u}{u^{2}+k^{2}}+\frac1k\tan^{-1}\frac{u}{k}\right]\) gives \(a=\frac{4}{3\sqrt3}\) and \(b=\frac13\). Hence \(9(\sqrt3\,a+b)=9\left(\frac43+\frac13\right)=15\).
authoredSolutions.89: A six-digit palindrome \(\overline{abccba}\) (with \(a\neq0\)) is automatically divisible by 11, since its alternating digit sum is \(a-b+c-c+b-a=0\). Divisibility by 5 needs the last digit \(a\in\{0,5\}\); as \(a\neq0\), \(a=5\). With \(b,c\) each free (10 ways), the count is \(10\times10=100\).
